ownerThemes.theme: A PatternReview owner who moved from domestic machines for bag making notes she no longer hand cranks through bulky seams; another says the servo motor makes speed very controllable.

New-to-industrial buyers on PatternReview ask whether the DDL-8700 can be sewn slowly and whether it will hold up to leather coats; replies steer them to servo motors and to the -H heavy variant for thick work.
Quiltingboard members recommend the servo motor and point out the head takes standard high shank feet, with bobbins and needles easy to buy online.
A Backpacking Light thread covers upgrading a clutch-motor 8700 to a servo for quieter, slower gear sewing.

editorial.verdict: Straight-stitch industrial head that Juki classes as medium-weight: owners praise the build, but it needs a table, a motor and floor space, and heavy leather is -H territory.
editorial.whoFor: Bag makers, gear sewers and small production shops who sew straight seams all day and want speed, a knee lift and an oil-bath hook.
editorial.skipIf: You need a portable machine, any stitch besides straight, or you expect it to sew heavy leather; Juki positions the DDL-8700H variant for heavy weight.
editorial.keySpec: 5,500 spm (base) · straight stitch · DBx1 needle · table + motor required
strengths: Owners report solid build and smooth running, with 6 of 7 build-quality voices positive.
Retailer reviewers often call it quiet; Juki's manual gives 83.5 dB(A) at 5,000 sti/min, a maker figure on paper.
Owners report standard feet, bobbins and DBx1 needles are easy to buy, and a free-motion foot worked for one owner.
weaknesses: Owners report recurring tension trouble, such as top thread showing underneath, though many of these are help-seeking Reddit threads.
Owners report setup and defect problems, such as a motor that ran backward at first and a bobbin that bunched when the needle did not stop up.
Owners report limits on thick or slippery work: one gets two layers of heavy waxed denim but thread snaps at three, and another could not sew split leather.

faqs.q: What do owners say about the Juki DDL-8700?
faqs.a: Across 60 Reddit threads and 2 retailer pages from 2010 to 2026, owners most often praise the build and the smooth, quiet running. Recurring complaints are tension and top-thread trouble on heavy thread, fabric limits on thick or grippy material, and motor faults. Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented.

faqs.q: What is the Juki DDL-8700 used for?
faqs.a: It is a straight-stitch, single-needle lockstitch machine. Juki's variant table calls the base DDL-8700 medium-weight, the 8700A light-weight and the 8700H heavy-weight. Owners report bag making, where one no longer hand cranks through bulky seams, and one owner says a lockstitch machine like it is unsuited to jersey because the stitch breaks when stretched.

faqs.q: How much does the Juki DDL-8700 cost?
faqs.a: Juki does not publish a price and sells through dealers. A Walmart marketplace listing with servo motor and table, assembly required, showed $999 on 2026-09-29, with a second listing at $899.99 and a DDL-8700-H listing at $1,004.40. Dealer bundles differ in what they include, so check the listing.

faqs.q: Can the Juki DDL-8700 sew leather?
faqs.a: Owner reports lean cautious. One owner could not sew split or deer leather, as the top thread frayed and snapped after about ten stitches despite heavy needles and bonded nylon thread. Buyers asking about leather coats are steered to a servo motor and to the -H heavy variant, which Juki lists as heavy-weight at 4,000 spm.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Juki DDL-8700, the -7 and the -H?
faqs.a: Per Juki's page the base DDL-8700 is medium-weight at 5,500 spm, the 8700A is light-weight and the 8700H is heavy-weight, both at 4,000 spm. The -7 is the trimmer variant per dealer and owner sources, since Juki's page names no trimmer on the base machine, and listings often mix the versions up. Marketplace titles pool these variants, so a quoted speed may belong to a different one [verify].

faqs.q: Does the Juki DDL-8700 come with a table and motor?
faqs.a: Not from the maker: it is sold as a head only. Dealer bundles add a table, stand, sewing light and a clutch or servo motor, so check what a listing includes. Sewing Machines Plus lists the table as shipped assembled.

faqs.q: Should I get a servo motor or a clutch motor on a Juki DDL-8700?
faqs.a: Owners on Quiltingboard and Backpacking Light recommend a servo for slow, controllable sewing, and one owner says the servo handles slow precision stitching through to very fast stitching. Another owner whose machine has a clutch motor says they want a servo. The servo has a speed dial under the table.

faqs.q: How fast is the Juki DDL-8700, and can it be slowed down?
faqs.a: Juki lists 5,500 stitches per minute for the base DDL-8700, while the DDL-8700A and DDL-8700H are 4,000. Slow control depends on the motor, and owners point to a servo with its speed dial.

faqs.q: What needles does the Juki DDL-8700 use?
faqs.a: Juki's page lists DB x 1 in sizes 9 to 18, with 14 as standard. The DDL-8700A uses DA x 1 and the DDL-8700H uses DB x 1 in sizes 19 to 23, so do not mix the variants up. One owner could not use the larger needle size wanted on heavy denim.
